rows.jp: 適当に部室で暇を潰して、教室に戻る途中。
rows.en: After killing time in the clubroom, I was on my way back to class.

ghs.en: After suitably passing time in the club room, I'm on my way back to the classroom.
ghs.assessment: The narrator kills time casually or aimlessly in the clubroom. 'Suitably passing time' suggests propriety or adequacy and is not idiomatic for this adverbial nuance.
ghs.remedy: Use 'After killing some time in the clubroom,'

rows.jp: 人気のない廊下で、処女がうずくまっていた。
rows.en: A virgin was crouched in the deserted hallway.

ghs.en: A maiden was crouching in a corridor devoid of human presence.
ghs.assessment: The narration bluntly labels the girl a virgin. 'Maiden' is an archaic euphemism that softens the comic directness and can mean merely an unmarried young woman.
ghs.remedy: Use the explicit noun 'virgin.'

rows.jp: 「大丈夫ですか、お嬢さん？」
rows.en: “Are you all right, miss?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Is everything well, ojou-san?"
ghs.assessment: The ordinary address 'miss' or 'young lady' is left as an unexplained romanized Japanese expression inside otherwise English dialogue.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Are you all right, miss?'

rows.jp: 尻に手を伸ばす。
rows.en: I reach for her butt.

ghs.en: I extended my hand towards her behind.

rows.jp: 「おっとぉ！」
rows.en: “Whoa!”

ghs.en: Girl: "Woh'tt'ooo!"
ghs.assessment: The surprised 'Whoa!' is rendered as an opaque apostrophe-heavy spelling that supplies no readable English pronunciation or meaningful source distinction.
ghs.remedy: Use an elongated 'Whoa!'

rows.jp: 瞬発力を発揮して、少女は立ち上がった。
rows.en: The girl shoots to her feet.

ghs.en: In a display of explosive force, the girl stood straight up,

rows.jp: すり足で距離を取る。
rows.en: I shuffle back to put some distance between us.

ghs.en: and gained distance with a suri-ashi.
ghs.assessment: The action is a sliding or shuffling step used to open distance. The untranslated technique term with an indefinite article leaves the motion inaccessible in English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'she slid back to put distance between us.'

rows.jp: 臨戦態勢に移行するのが早い。
rows.en: She is quick to shift into combat mode.

ghs.en: She's quick to transition into combat readiness.

rows.jp: しかも跳ね起きると同時に、俺に一撃を加えてきた。
rows.en: She even strikes me the instant she springs to her feet.

ghs.en: And, simultaneously with her springing up, she inflicted an attack on me.
ghs.assessment: She strikes the narrator as she springs up. The nominalized timing phrase and 'inflicted an attack' are unidiomatic calques that obscure a simple simultaneous blow.
ghs.remedy: Use 'As she sprang up, she struck me.'

highlights.text: simultaneously with her springing up, she inflicted an attack

rows.jp: 「……なかなかやるな」
rows.en: “……Not bad.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...nice one there, very nice."

rows.jp: 「せんぱいこそ」
rows.en: “Right back at you, Taichi.”

ghs.en: Girl: "Same to you, Senpai."

rows.jp: 片手で受け止めた、顔面を狙って放たれた雑巾を、静かに床に落とす。
rows.en: I catch the rag she flung at my face in one hand, then quietly let it fall to the floor.

ghs.en: The rag that she threw towards my face fell from the one hand I had caught it with to the floor, in silence.
ghs.assessment: The narrator deliberately and quietly drops the rag he caught. The English makes the rag fall from his hand and turns controlled action into an accidental event inside a malformed relative construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I quietly dropped the rag I'd caught in one hand.'

highlights.text: fell from the one hand I had caught it with

rows.jp: 「なんか久しぶりに会ったという気がするな」
rows.en: “Feels like I haven’t seen you in ages.”

rows.jp: 「そですね」
rows.en: “Sure does.”

ghs.en: Girl: "It has."

rows.jp: 映画化された某有名ファンタジー小説のヒロインみたいな少女が、立っている。
rows.en: Before me stands a girl who looks like the schoolgirl heroine from a certain famous fantasy novel adapted for film.

ghs.en: This girl so like the heroine of that famous fantasy novel adapted to the big screen stands up.
ghs.assessment: The girl is standing there and resembles the heroine of a well-known fantasy novel adapted for film. The English is grammatically malformed and changes the static description into the action of standing up.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A girl resembling the heroine of a famous fantasy novel turned movie stood before me.'

highlights.text: This girl so like the heroine of that famous fantasy novel adapted to the big screen stands up.

rows.jp: 安心していい。外見だけだ。
rows.en: Don’t worry. The resemblance ends with her looks.

ghs.en: Be at ease. That's just her looks.

rows.jp: 「しばらく会ってないからって名前とか忘れてへんで？」
rows.en: “Don’t think I forgot your name just ’cause it’s been a while.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Would it be strange if I said that we haven't met in a long enough while that I forgot your name and the like?"
ghs.assessment: The source assures her that he has not forgotten her name merely because they have not met for a while. The English reverses this into a hypothetical confession that he did forget it.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It's not like I forgot your name just because we haven't seen each other for a while.'

highlights.text: Would it be strange if I said that we haven't met in a long enough while that I forgot your name and the like

rows.jp: 「やー」
rows.en: “Nooo.”

ghs.en: Girl: "Naaah."

rows.jp: 「だから安心してくれ……」
rows.en: “So you can relax……”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, but be at ease..."

rows.jp: 「ジョンソン」
rows.en: “Johnson.”

rows.jp: 「せめて女性の名前で」
rows.en: “At least make it a woman’s name.”

ghs.en: Girl: "At least use a girl's name."

rows.jp: 外人なのはもういい、という顔をしていた。
rows.en: Her face said she had given up objecting to the foreign name.

ghs.en: A face one could say had had enough of being thought foreign.

rows.jp: 「腕をあげたな、美希」
rows.en: “You’ve improved, Miki.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You've improved your skills, Miki."

rows.jp: 「ええ」
rows.en: “Yes.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Yep."

rows.jp: 山辺美希は涙を誘うほど乏しい胸を張った。
rows.en: Miki Yamanobe thrust out a chest so meager it could bring a tear to your eye.

ghs.en: Yamanobe Miki stuck out a chest so unplentiful it invites tears.
ghs.assessment: The joke describes a chest so meager it brings tears. 'Unplentiful' is an unnatural and weak adjective that obscures the blunt visual insult.
ghs.remedy: Use 'a chest so meager it could move you to tears.'

rows.jp: 「わたしのお尻は高いですから」
rows.en: “My butt doesn’t come cheap.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Because my behind is valuable."

rows.jp: 「ちょっと触れたけどね」
rows.en: “I did get a little feel.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Although I managed just to graze it."

rows.jp: 「サービスです」
rows.en: “That was a free sample.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Fanservice."

rows.jp: 動じない。
rows.en: Unfazed.

ghs.en: Unperturbed.

rows.jp: 「だがそのスカートのめくれまでは……」
rows.en: “But surely the way your skirt flipped up...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But until I flip that skirt..."
ghs.assessment: The fragment refers to the skirt having flipped up, continuing a bluff about what just happened. The English makes it a future deliberate action by the speaker.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But your skirt did flip up—'

rows.jp: 「めくれてません（きっぱり）」
rows.en: “It did not flip up,” she says flatly.

ghs.en: Miki: "You shan't flip. (Decisevely)"
ghs.assessment: She firmly states that the skirt did not flip up. The English instead commands a future subject not to flip, omits the skirt, and misspells the manner note.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It didn't flip up. (Firmly.)'

rows.jp: やるな。
rows.en: She is good.

ghs.en: Not bad.

rows.jp: ハッタリもきかなくなったか。
rows.en: So my bluffs do not work on her anymore.

ghs.en: Bluffs are no longer effective, then?

rows.jp: 「いいだろう。今回は花を持たせておく」
rows.en: “Very well. I’ll let you have this round.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But it's fine. For this once, I'll let you carry the flowers so that you can take credit for this."
ghs.assessment: The idiom means letting the other person have the credit or glory this time. The English retains a meaningless literal image and then redundantly explains it.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Fine. I'll let you have this one.'

rows.jp: 「えへ」
rows.en: “Eheh.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Eheh!"

rows.jp: にっこりと笑った。
rows.en: She beams at me.

ghs.en: She smiled brightly.

rows.jp: うわー、抱きしめてぇ。
rows.en: God, I want to hug her.

ghs.en: Waaah, hug meee!
ghs.assessment: The narrator exclaims that he wants to hug her. The English turns that desire into a command or plea for someone else to hug him, reversing the action's direction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'God, I wanna hug her.'

rows.jp: 「なにしてたんだ？　掃除ごっこか？」
rows.en: “What were you doing? Playing at cleaning?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Watcha doing? Playing cleaning lady?"

rows.jp: 「あ、はい、なんかここんとこ汚れてて」
rows.en: “Oh, yeah. It’s been kind of dirty around here lately.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Ah, yes, things are a bit dirty lately."

rows.jp: 「あっし、きれい好き」
rows.en: “Me, I like things clean.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Me, ah' like 'em clean."

rows.jp: 架空の力こぶを作る。
rows.en: She flexes an imaginary bicep.

ghs.en: She flexes an Imaginary bicep.

rows.jp: 「自発的にかい、そいつはクールだネ！」
rows.en: “Taking the initiative, are we? How cool!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "All of your own initiative, that is very cool yes!"
ghs.assessment: The mock-praise asks whether she did it voluntarily and calls that cool. The English is a fragment followed by an unnatural declarative tag, losing the question's shape.
ghs.remedy: Use 'All on your own initiative? That's very cool!'

highlights.text: All of your own initiative, that is very cool yes

rows.jp: 「……あー、わかったわかった、皆まで言うなよマイスウィート。しょうがないな、サインだろ？」
rows.en: “……Ah, I get it, I get it. Say no more, my sweet. Fine—an autograph, right?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...ahhh, I get it, I get it, say nothing further my sweet! There's no way, it's about my autograph, right? You desire the autograph of this Ijuin Taichi here. You've merely engaged in the good manners typical of our chosen career path and made a demand in ways roundabout."

rows.jp: 「この伊集院太一のサインが欲しいと。我が進路で良俗に従事することで遠回しに催促していたわけだ」
rows.en: “You wanted the autograph of the great Taichi Ijūin. By laboring for public decency along my route, you were begging for it without saying a word.”

rows.jp: 「……あーあー……アレですか」
rows.en: “...Ohhh... Is that what this is?”

ghs.en: Miki: "...ahh, yeah... that one, yes."

rows.jp: 「なんか久々ですねえー」
rows.en: “It's been a while, huh?”

ghs.en: Miki: "Really been a long while there."
ghs.assessment: The casual observation that it feels like a long time is recognizable, but the English omits a subject and finite auxiliary and appends an unnatural 'there.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'It really has been a while, hasn't it?'

highlights.text: Really been a long while there

rows.jp: なんとも切なそうな顔をする。
rows.en: Her face turns unbearably wistful.

ghs.en: She makes a face that looks very pained.

rows.jp: というか泣きそうではないか。
rows.en: Wait, is she about to cry?

ghs.en: Or should I say, isn't she as if about to cry?

rows.jp: というか泣きそうではないか。
rows.en: Wait, is she about to cry?

ghs.en: Or should I say, isn't she as if about to cry?

rows.jp: 二回も思ってしまったぞ。
rows.en: I had the exact same thought twice.

ghs.en: I even thought that twice dammit.

rows.jp: 焦ってはいかん、冷静に対処するのだ。
rows.en: Don’t panic. Handle this calmly.

ghs.en: Getting flustered is a no go, cope with this with composure.
ghs.assessment: The instruction to handle the situation calmly is accurate in content, but the repeated preposition and clinical 'cope' produce an unidiomatic calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Don't panic. Handle this calmly.'

rows.jp: 酸いも甘いも噛みわけたエリートヤングアダルト候補生として！
rows.en: As an elite young-adult trainee who knows life's bitter and sweet!

ghs.en: Like an elite cadet of young adulthood who is experienced in the ways of the world, having tasted both its bitter and its sweet!

rows.jp: 「どどどどどどうしたことだ、山辺君！　そんなに嫌であれば無理に余白を潰そうなんて思わないぞ！　正直に申告するのダっ！？」
rows.en: “W-w-w-w-what’s wrong, Ms. Yamanobe? If you hate it that much, I won’t insist on filling all those blank pages! Tell me honestly!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wh-wh-wh-wh-wh-what is wrong, Yamanobe-kun?! If that is so disagreeable, than I shall not even think to wast that blank space! I proclaim this with honesty, see?!"
ghs.assessment: The speaker commands her to report her feelings honestly. The English changes the addressee's required confession into the speaker proclaiming his own honesty; surrounding spelling and conjunction errors further damage the line.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tell me honestly!'

rows.jp: 声震えまくり。
rows.en: My voice is shaking like mad.

ghs.en: My voice just shakes.
ghs.assessment: The source says his voice is trembling violently or all over, not merely that it shakes. The English drops the emphatic degree and shifts into an oddly generic present.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My voice was shaking like crazy.'

rows.jp: 「おお、泣いてる、あわわ」
rows.en: “Oh, you're crying—oh no, oh no.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, she's crying, ahWahWah!"

rows.jp: 目尻をぬぐう。
rows.en: She wipes the corner of her eye.

ghs.en: She wipes the corners of her eyes,

rows.jp: 俺もつられて泣きそう。
rows.en: Now I’m about to cry too.

ghs.en: which carries me to tearfulness as well.
ghs.assessment: The narrator feels like crying in sympathy. 'Carries me to tearfulness' is an abstract and nonidiomatic rendering of emotional contagion.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Now I feel like crying too.'

rows.jp: 「あ、いえ、なんでもありません、サー」
rows.en: “Oh, no. It’s nothing, sir.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Ah, no, it's nothing, SAH!"

rows.jp: 「涙腺からちょっと、青春汁が、漏れて……」
rows.en: “Just a little…… youth juice leaking out of my tear ducts……”

ghs.en: Miki: "It's just that my lachrymal glands leaked some adolescent juice..."

rows.jp: 「なんだ……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Whoa..."

rows.jp: 青春汁か。
rows.en: Youth juice.

ghs.en: Adolescent juice then.

rows.jp: 「驚かすない」
rows.en: “Don’t scare me like that.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't scare me then."

rows.jp: 冷や汗をぬぐった。
rows.en: I wipe away the cold sweat.

ghs.en: I wiped off cold sweat.
ghs.assessment: The action is clear, but English requires a possessive or determiner for the sweat being wiped away; the bare mass-noun construction reads as a calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I wiped the cold sweat from my brow.'

rows.jp: 「じゃあ今回は王子（俺）のサインはおあずけだな」
rows.en: “Then the prince's autograph—mine—will have to wait this time.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well then, this time the Autograph of the Prince (me) is postponed."
ghs.assessment: The mock-prince persona says she will have to wait for his autograph this time. The nominalized passive and arbitrary capitalization are not natural English dialogue.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Then you'll have to wait for your prince's autograph.'

highlights.text: the Autograph of the Prince (me) is postponed

rows.jp: 「いえ！」
rows.en: “No!”

ghs.en: Miki: "NO!"

rows.jp: 喉のかすれるような悲鳴。
rows.en: A hoarse little shriek catches in her throat.

ghs.en: A shriek as if her throat was hoarse.

rows.jp: 「いります！　してください！」
rows.en: “I want it! Please do it!”

ghs.en: Miki: "I need you in this! Do this please!"
ghs.assessment: She says she wants the autograph and asks him to do it. The English instead says she needs him 'in this,' inventing an object relationship and producing an unintelligible request.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I want it! Please do it!'

rows.jp: 「そ、そんなにしてほしいのかね？」
rows.en: “Y-you want me to do it that badly?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Y, you want this done to you that badly?"

rows.jp: こっちがたじろぐ。
rows.en: Now I’m the one recoiling.

ghs.en: Faltering from my direction.
ghs.assessment: The narrator says he is the one who recoils or falters. The English removes the person as subject and substitutes a direction, leaving a sentence fragment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Now I was the one who recoiled.'

rows.jp: 「してください、してください」
rows.en: “Please do it. Please do it.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Do this please! Do this please!"

rows.jp: 甲高い声で『してください』と連呼される。
rows.en: She keeps repeating “Please do it” in a high-pitched voice.

ghs.en: I'm repeatedly called to "do this please" with a shrill voice.
ghs.assessment: He is subjected to the shrill repetition of the quoted plea. 'Called to do this please' converts the words into an indirect summons and is not grammatical English reporting.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She kept shrilling, Please do it, over and over.'

rows.jp: 下腹部が熱くなってきた。
rows.en: Heat begins to gather below my belt.

ghs.en: The lower abdomen grew hotter.
ghs.assessment: The contextually understood body part is the narrator's own lower abdomen. The English turns it into a generic anatomical object and loses the personal bodily reaction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My lower abdomen was getting hot.'

rows.jp: どうしてだろう？
rows.en: Why?

ghs.en: But why, really?

rows.jp: どうしてなんだろう？
rows.en: Why is that?

ghs.en: For what reason, even?

rows.jp: かいめんたいはいつもぼくの意志をむしして、あばれるんだ―――
rows.en: The little sea sponge always ignores what I want and runs wild―――

ghs.en: Why must the erectile tissue of this innocent young boy ignore my volition and just rage---

rows.jp: 童話調に思考しても生々しさは消えなかった。
rows.en: Even thinking in fairy-tale prose does nothing to make it feel less raw.

ghs.en: I may have thought this in the tone of a fairy-tale, but the graphicness didn't go away.
ghs.assessment: The contrast between fairy-tale framing and persistent visceral immediacy is retained, but 'graphicness' is an awkward abstract coinage that does not naturally express 生々しさ here.
ghs.remedy: Use 'the visceral reality of it didn't go away.'

rows.jp: 「わ、わかった、ではアレを」
rows.en: “F-fine. Then bring it out.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I-, I got that, well then 'that' I'll do."
ghs.assessment: The stammered acceptance and turn toward the euphemistic 'that' are visible, but the English is syntactically inverted and over-completes the source fragment with an awkward 'I'll do.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'O-okay. Then, that...'

highlights.text: I-, I got that, well then 'that' I'll do.

rows.jp: 「はい」
rows.en: “Yes.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Here!"

rows.jp: 美希は垂直な胸元をまさぐって、メイトブックを出した。
rows.en: Miki rummages around at the sheer vertical plane of her chest and produces her Mate Book.

ghs.en: Miki groped about her perpendicular chest, then produced her MateBook.

rows.jp: 当校では身分証明書をかねるこの手帳を、そう呼ぶ。
rows.en: That is what our school calls this handbook, which doubles as student identification.

ghs.en: So it is called at this school, this ID booklet with a second role.
ghs.assessment: The source says that this notebook, which doubles as identification, is called that at the school. 'An ID booklet with a second role' reverses which function is being specified and leaves the other role unexplained.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's what our school calls this notebook, which doubles as an ID.'

highlights.text: So it is called at this school, this ID booklet with a second role.

rows.jp: そう。
rows.en: Yes.

ghs.en: Yes.

rows.jp: どうも本校のお歴々は、『都会』の駅裏にある人気ＮＯ１高級浴場『メイトブック』の存在を知らないようなのだ。
rows.en: Apparently, the venerable authorities at our school have never heard of Mate Book, the number-one luxury bathhouse tucked behind the station in “the City.”

ghs.en: No dignitary of this school would be unaware of the existence of MateBook, the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station.
ghs.assessment: The source says the school's leading figures apparently do not know of the bathhouse. The English reverses that into a claim that none could be unaware, and also invents a 'popular spot' not present in the location phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Apparently, the school's grandees don't know about MateBook, the number-one luxury bathhouse behind the station in the City.'

highlights.text: No dignitary of this school would be unaware of the existence of MateBook, the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station.

rows.jp: 会員になると手帳を渡され、一回ご利用するごとに姫のスタンプがもらえる。
rows.en: Members receive a booklet, and every visit earns them a stamp from one of the ladies.

ghs.en: A notebook is given on gaining membership, and for every use a Princess Stamp is received.

rows.jp: スタンプを集めることによって、Ｗやトリプルなどのサービスが格安で楽しめるという寸法だ。
rows.en: Collect enough stamps and you can enjoy double or even triple services at bargain prices.

ghs.en: The accumulation of stamps is the measure of how cheaply one can enjoy services such as the Double or the Triple.
ghs.assessment: Collecting stamps enables discounted access to the named services. The English instead makes the number of stamps a measure of relative cheapness, changing the mechanism into a scale.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Collect enough stamps and you can enjoy services like the Double or Triple at a steep discount.'

highlights.text: The accumulation of stamps is the measure of how cheaply one can enjoy services such as the Double or the Triple.

rows.jp: ……トリプルだなんて。
rows.en: ……Triple.

ghs.en: ...what's even a triple now.
ghs.assessment: The fragment reacts in astonishment to a 'Triple, of all things.' The English turns that reaction into a request for the term's definition.
ghs.remedy: Use '...A Triple, of all things.'

rows.jp: それはいかなる世界なのか。
rows.en: What manner of world could that be?

ghs.en: What kind of world would be that?
ghs.assessment: The question's content is correct, but its English word order is unidiomatic.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What kind of world would that be?'

highlights.text: What kind of world would be that?

rows.jp: 桃源郷なのか。
rows.en: An earthly paradise?

ghs.en: Would it be Shangri-la?

rows.jp: 大陽は黄色いのか。
rows.en: Is the sun yellow there?

ghs.en: And is the sun yellow?

rows.jp: 勃ってきました……。
rows.en: I’m getting hard……

ghs.en: I have erected...
ghs.assessment: The source says the speaker is becoming erect. 'I have erected' makes him the transitive agent of an unstated object and is not idiomatic English for the bodily state.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'm getting hard...'

rows.jp: いかん。
rows.en: This is bad.

ghs.en: This is bad!

rows.jp: ここで安易に前傾シフトをとれば、美希にばれる。
rows.en: If I take the easy way out and hunch forward now, Miki will see right through me.

ghs.en: If I take a gentle forwards Shift here, Miki will notice.
ghs.assessment: The risk of giving himself away by casually leaning forward is retained, but 'take a gentle forwards Shift' is an unnatural mechanical calque and the capitalization is unjustified.
ghs.remedy: Use 'If I casually shift forward now, Miki will notice.'

rows.jp: 美希は処女だが、男の生理には精通している。
rows.en: Miki may be a virgin, but she knows all about how the male body works.

ghs.en: Miki might be a literal maiden, but she is acquainted with male physiology,
ghs.assessment: The concessive states that she is a virgin despite knowing male physiology well. 'Might be' introduces uncertainty absent from the source, while 'literal maiden' substitutes an archaic euphemism for the factual contrast.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Miki may be a virgin, but she knows male physiology inside out.'

rows.jp: 俺が教えたから。
rows.en: Because I taught her.

ghs.en: because I explained it to her.

rows.jp: 前傾しなくともばれるだろうが、堂々としていれば、格好だけはつく。
rows.en: She'll probably notice whether I hunch forward or not, but if I brazen it out, I can at least keep up appearances.

ghs.en: Even if I don't lean I'll likely be spotted, but if I stay confident, I should at least look cool.
ghs.assessment: The source says brazenly acting as though nothing is wrong will at least preserve appearances. 'Stay confident' and 'look cool' turn that social cover into self-confidence and attractiveness.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She'll probably notice even if I don't lean forward, but if I brazen it out, I can at least keep up appearances.'

highlights.text: if I stay confident, I should at least look cool

ghs.en: Miki: "..."

rows.jp: あ、今ちらっと見た。
rows.en: Oh. She just snuck a glance.

ghs.en: Ah, she glimpsed right then.
ghs.assessment: The source observes that she just stole a glance. 'Glimpsed' is used transitively without an object and 'right then' weakens the immediate 'just now.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ah, she just glanced over.'

rows.jp: 美希、やや赤面。
rows.en: Miki blushes slightly.

ghs.en: Miki's face goes fairly red.

rows.jp: なにも言わない。
rows.en: She says nothing.

ghs.en: She says nothing.

rows.jp: 視線を窓の外に向けて、わずかにもじもじする。
rows.en: She turns to look out the window, fidgeting ever so slightly.

ghs.en: She turns her gaze towards the outside via the window, and fidgets slightly.
ghs.assessment: The action of looking out the window and fidgeting slightly is present, but the route-like phrase 'towards the outside via the window' is not natural visual description.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She turns her gaze out the window and fidgets slightly.'

highlights.text: towards the outside via the window

rows.jp: うわ、かえって恥ずかしい。なにか言えや。
rows.en: Ugh, this is even more embarrassing. Say something already.

ghs.en: Wah, this is even more embarrassing! Say something!

rows.jp: いっそ言葉で俺を玩弄(がんろう)してくれ。
rows.en: Go on, toy with me—just use words.

ghs.en: Please make sport of me with words instead!

rows.jp: 羞恥のあまり、荒ぶる破壊神は鎮まっていく。
rows.en: The raging god of destruction subsides beneath the weight of my shame.

ghs.en: But the embarrasment is so great that this savage god of destruction grows subdued.
ghs.assessment: The metaphorical content is retained, but 'embarrassment' is misspelled in the displayed prose.
ghs.remedy: Correct 'embarrasment' to 'embarrassment.'

rows.jp: 実戦経験がないためか、直で面すると弱いんだな。
rows.en: Maybe having no firsthand experience is why she falters when confronted with the real thing.

ghs.en: As a consequence of a lack of combat experience, perhaps, direct confrontation is a weakness.
ghs.assessment: The source infers that she is weak when confronted directly, perhaps because she lacks practical experience. The English depersonalizes her into the abstract claim that confrontation itself is a weakness and places 'perhaps' unnaturally.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Maybe because she has no practical experience, she's weak when faced with the real thing.'

highlights.text: As a consequence of a lack of combat experience, perhaps, direct confrontation is a weakness.

rows.jp: 直ハラ禁止だ。
rows.en: No hands-on harassment.

ghs.en: Directassment prohibited.

rows.jp: ※直ハラ――
rows.en: *Hands-on harassment――

ghs.en:
* Directassment = Taichian for the Direct
Performance of Sex-related Harassment.

rows.jp: 太一語。直接行う性的いやがらせ。主に性器を露出し異性に接触させるなどの小児的猥褻行為。ちょんまげ、爆破スイッチ、一本釣り、等。状況によっては痴漢行為と見なされることもある。
rows.en: Taichi-speak. Sexual harassment committed through direct physical action. Chiefly childish acts of indecency in which one exposes the genitals and makes contact with a member of the opposite sex: the topknot, the detonator, the pole-and-line, and so on. Depending on the circumstances, these acts may be considered molestation.

rows.jp: というか全部、完璧に、申し分のない、痴漢行為である。
rows.en: Or rather, every last one is unambiguously, incontrovertibly an act of molestation.

ghs.en: Or should I say that they all are flawlessly unquestionably molestation.
ghs.assessment: The conclusion that all the listed acts are unequivocally molestation is present, but the stacked adverbs are unpunctuated and 'are ... molestation' is not grammatical count syntax.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Or rather, every last one is a perfectly unambiguous act of molestation.'

highlights.text: Or should I say that they all are flawlessly unquestionably molestation.

rows.jp: 「美希は手帳だいぶ使いこんでるなあ。ぼろぼろだ」
rows.en: “You’ve gotten a lot of use out of this book, Miki. It’s falling apart.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You've been using this notebook thoroughly, Miki. It's all worn!"
ghs.assessment: The source observes that she has used the notebook heavily and that it is in tatters. 'Using ... thoroughly' is an unnatural calque, and 'all worn' weakens the physical condition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You've really put this notebook through its paces, Miki. It's falling apart.'

rows.jp: 「ぼろぼろ」
rows.en: “Falling apart.”

ghs.en: Miki: "All worn."

rows.jp: 無意味に繰り返すことで肯定する美希。
rows.en: Miki agrees by pointlessly repeating me.

ghs.en: Miki assents by meaninglessly repeating my words.

rows.jp: ページを繰ると、メモ欄にはすでに俺のサインがでかでかと書かれていた。
rows.en: I flip through the pages and find my signature already scrawled in huge letters across the notes section.

ghs.en: Flipping the pages, I see annotation fields filled with my large-sized signature.
ghs.assessment: The source reveals that his signature is already written very large in the memo field. The English pluralizes the field, makes it generally filled, and uses the unnatural adjective 'large-sized.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'As I flipped through it, I found my signature already scrawled huge across the memo field.'

highlights.text: annotation fields filled with my large-sized signature

rows.jp: 何ページにも渡っている。
rows.en: The signatures fill page after page.

ghs.en: I pass by several pages.
ghs.assessment: The source says the oversized signature extends across several pages. The English instead describes the narrator moving past pages, changing both subject and action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It stretched across several pages.'

rows.jp: 俺のサインをコレクトしているかのようだ。
rows.en: It's almost as though she's collecting my autographs.

ghs.en: It's as if she were collecting my signatures.

rows.jp: 正確には、俺がコレクトさせているわけですが。
rows.en: Strictly speaking, I’m the one making her collect them.

ghs.en: Or, to be precise, this is me making her collect them.

rows.jp: 白紙を見つけ、そこに新たなサインを書き込む。
rows.en: I find a blank page and add a fresh signature.

ghs.en: I find a blank page and there I fill out a fresh signature.
ghs.assessment: The action of finding a blank page and adding a new signature is present, but English speakers write or sign a signature rather than 'fill out' one.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I find a blank page and write a fresh signature on it.'

ghs.en: Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 「あのさ、今回は俺がサインしたくて美希の胸を借りたってことで……全然いじわるしようとか思ってないからね？」
rows.en: “Look, this time I wanted to sign it, and I was only borrowing your chest as a writing surface…… I wasn’t trying to be mean to you at all, okay?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You know, this little game of ours here was just because I wanted to put my autograph on your chest padding... not because of mean intent, OK?"
ghs.assessment: The speaker proposes framing the incident as borrowing her chest because he wanted to sign, then denies intending to tease her. The English invents a shared 'game,' changes the object into padding, and turns the strained excuse into a different proposition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Look, let's just say I borrowed your chest because I wanted somewhere to sign this time... I wasn't trying to be mean, okay?'

highlights.text: this little game of ours here was just because I wanted to put my autograph on your chest padding

rows.jp: 「嫌がってないですってば」
rows.en: “I keep telling you, I don’t mind.”

ghs.en: Miki: "I'm telling you I didn't dislike it."

rows.jp: 「そ、そう？」
rows.en: “R-really?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You-, don't?"
ghs.assessment: The stammered response is simply 'R-really?' or 'I-is that so?' The English instead forces a grammatically broken negative echo of the previous sentence.
ghs.remedy: Use 'R-really?'

rows.jp: サインを書き終える。
rows.en: I finish signing.

ghs.en: I finished writing my signature.

rows.jp: 美希はおだやかな顔をしていた。
rows.en: Miki wears a calm expression.

ghs.en: Miki was making a tranquil face.
ghs.assessment: The calm expression is understood, but 'making a tranquil face' is an unnatural English calque for wearing or having that expression.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Miki wore a peaceful expression.'

rows.jp: 確かに嫌がっている風ではない。
rows.en: She certainly doesn't seem bothered.

ghs.en: There's certainly not a whiff of pretense of having disliked it.
ghs.assessment: The source says she certainly does not look displeased. The English instead denies any pretense of having disliked it, shifting from her apparent feeling to whether that feeling is feigned and producing the opposite logical structure.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She certainly doesn't look bothered.'

highlights.text: There's certainly not a whiff of pretense of having disliked it.

rows.jp: 他のページをざっと調べる。
rows.en: I skim the other pages.

ghs.en: I quickly check out the rest of the pages.

rows.jp: 「あー、別にデートの約束とか書いてないんで」
rows.en: “Oh, I didn’t write anything about a date or anything.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Ah, I don't really write my dating plans or anything there."

rows.jp: 「あっそ」
rows.en: “Oh.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah well."

rows.jp: 手帳を返す。
rows.en: I hand the book back.

ghs.en: I return the notebook.

rows.jp: スリッパの底みたいな胸元に抱きかかえて、
rows.en: She hugs it to her chest, flat as the sole of a slipper, and says,

ghs.en: She holds it against a chest so like the bottom of a slipper.

rows.jp: 「ご安心ください。美希は処女でございます～」
rows.en: “Please rest assured: Miki remains a virgin~”

ghs.en: Miki: "Please be at ease. Miki most certainly is still a virgi～n!"

rows.jp: 「べ、別にそんなことで安心したりしないもん」
rows.en: “I-it’s not like that makes me feel better or anything.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It-, it's not like you need to reassure me of such things!"
ghs.assessment: The speaker protests that this fact does not make him feel relieved. The English instead tells her that she does not need to reassure him, changing the subject and the force of the embarrassed denial.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I-it's not like that makes me feel relieved or anything!'

highlights.text: it's not like you need to reassure me of such things

rows.jp: うろたえると俺、小児化。
rows.en: When I get flustered, I regress into a child.

ghs.en: Flustered, I regress to childhood.

rows.jp: 「はいはい、わかっております」

ghs.en: Miki: "Yes, yes, I do understand."
